input:
AI infrastructure spending is going to keep compounding for at least another
   two years. The constraint isn't demand, it's power and packaging capacity, and
   the companies that own those bottlenecks capture the margin. I want exposure to
   that but I don't want to be wiped out if the capex cycle turns.

thesis.title: AI Infrastructure Bottleneck Capture
thesis.summary: Hyperscaler AI capex continues to compound because demand for inference and training exceeds supply of power-dense packaging and interconnect. The companies that own those physical bottlenecks — advanced packaging, high-bandwidth silicon, networking — capture margin that software players cannot. NVDA owns the GPU and NVLink stack; AVGO owns custom silicon and SerDes interconnect that hyperscalers use to reduce NVDA dependency while still spending. The S&P 500 anchor absorbs the scenario where the capex cycle turns without warning, limiting drawdown without requiring a directional call on macro.

holdings.rationale: NVIDIA's CUDA moat and NVLink fabric mean hyperscalers must route the majority of AI compute spend through NVDA hardware. GPU scarcity is a supply constraint NVDA controls via TSMC allocation, not a demand problem. This is the most direct expression of the bottleneck thesis.

Broadcom's custom ASIC business (Google TPU, Meta MTIA) and SerDes interconnect are the primary alternative to NVDA for hyperscalers. More capex spent on custom silicon flows directly to AVGO's networking and packaging revenue, making it a second-order bottleneck beneficiary with less multiple risk than NVDA.

Provides the capex-cycle hedge the investor explicitly requested. If AI infrastructure spending reverses, SPY's diversification across sectors that are not correlated to hyperscaler capex absorbs the blow. Also satisfies the core liquidity floor without adding a filler position.

The Nasdaq 100 carries the surviving AI beneficiaries (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, NVDA, AVGO) at index weight, giving passive exposure to the capex cycle without single-stock concentration. If NVDA's packaging thesis plays out sector-wide, QQQ captures spillover into hyperscalers that are both spenders and beneficiaries.

falsifier.claim: Hyperscaler AI capex continues to grow year-over-year, sustaining demand for advanced packaging and interconnect that NVDA and AVGO supply.
falsifier.observable: Combined capex guidance from Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet on their next four quarterly earnings calls.
falsifier.breachCondition: Any two of the three companies guide full-year capex flat or down year-over-year in the same earnings cycle.
